description.zh: 免费希腊神测试：18道原创选择比较宙斯、雅典娜、阿波罗、阿芙罗狄蒂、阿瑞斯和阿尔忒弥斯。无需注册，全部最高并列与完整说明直接读；神话趣味，不鉴定能力、天命或职业。
description.en: Which Greek god are you? Compare six myth themes through 18 original choices. Read full results and highest ties free, without signup or ability claims.

seoTitle.zh: 希腊神测试：18题、六位神祇与完整结果
seoTitle.en: Which Greek God Are You? Free Quiz and Full Results

introduction.zh: 你更想明确共同约定、比较路线、创作表达、体验美感交流、试一个小挑战，还是自主观察？本版从六位希腊神话人物中选取当代偏好联想，提供18道普通、低风险的原创四选一。全部完成后看六主题原始次数，最高并列都保留完整报告。名字只是娱乐标签，不是古代完整人格分类，更不说明谁更聪明、勇敢、有魅力或适合某种职业；神话性别不限制匹配。六份完整结果也可以先读。
introduction.en: Would you rather clarify shared agreements, compare routes, make an expression, enjoy aesthetic connection, try a bounded challenge or observe at your own pace? This edition uses six selected Greek myth figures for contemporary preference associations in 18 original, low-stakes choices. After completion, compare raw counts and read every highest-tied report in full. Names are entertainment labels, not a complete ancient personality system or evidence of intelligence, courage, charm or career fit. Mythological genders restrict no one’s matches. All six full guides are also available before answering.

instructions.zh: 本版选取六位希腊神话人物作娱乐主题标签，不是古代完整人格分类，也不测神话知识。按你目前更想选择的做法回答18题；每题只提供其中四种选择，每个主题在全卷出现12次，在四个位置各3次。所有情境都是普通、自愿、可退出的安排；没有道德上唯一正确或证明勇气的选项。全部选择后看本题组相对计数，保留全部最高并列。名字和性别不限制谁可以匹配；结果不判断真实能力、信仰身份、天命、精神状态或职业适配。
instructions.en: This edition uses six selected Greek myth figures as entertainment labels, not a complete ancient personality system or a mythology knowledge test. Answer 18 questions with the approach you currently prefer. Each offers four themes; every theme appears 12 times and three times in each position. Situations are ordinary, voluntary and open to withdrawal, without morally superior answers or proof of courage. After completion, compare counts within this set and retain every highest tie. Names and genders restrict no one’s matches. Results establish no ability, religious identity, destiny, mental state or career fit.

雅典娜：比较路径与计划

prompt.zh: 社区自愿征集一个小展览的想法，你最想贡献哪一部分？
prompt.en: A community invites voluntary ideas for a small exhibition. Which contribution would you most like to make?

label.zh: 和参与者约定展览范围，承担协调已同意事项的责任。
label.en: Agree the exhibition’s scope with participants and coordinate what was agreed.

label.zh: 比较两种布置方案，标出各自的条件和取舍。
label.en: Compare two layouts and mark the conditions and tradeoffs of each.

label.zh: 为展览写一小段声音或文字，让主题有自己的节奏。
label.en: Write a short sound or text piece that gives the theme its own rhythm.

label.zh: 选择彼此衬托的颜色和欢迎语，让入口更有亲近感。
label.en: Choose complementary colours and a welcoming message for the entrance.

prompt.zh: 雨天有一段自己支配的空闲，你更想怎样度过？
prompt.en: You have some freely chosen time on a rainy day. Which way of spending it appeals most?

label.zh: 拿一个感兴趣的小问题，画出几种解决路线。
label.en: Take an interesting small problem and sketch several ways to approach it.

label.zh: 听一段喜欢的旋律，再尝试自己的短小变奏。
label.en: Listen to a melody I enjoy and try a small variation of my own.

label.zh: 整理一个自己喜欢的角落，享受色彩和物件的搭配。
label.en: Arrange a corner I like and enjoy the combination of colours and objects.

label.zh: 选一个安全、可暂停的小练习，试着完成其中一轮。
label.en: Choose a safe exercise I can pause and try completing one round.

prompt.zh: 要留下这段日常生活的一份纪念，你更想做什么？
prompt.en: You want to keep a small record of this period of everyday life. What would you prefer to make?

label.zh: 写几行有个人语气的文字，或录一段短短的声音。
label.en: Write a few lines in my own voice or record a short sound piece.

label.zh: 挑出让自己感到美好的细节，编成一页图文。
label.en: Choose details I find beautiful and arrange them on a page.

label.zh: 记下一次自愿练习里从开始到完成的具体过程。
label.en: Record the concrete steps of a voluntary practice from beginning to completion.

label.zh: 按自己的节奏观察天气或窗边植物，留下几条记录。
label.en: Observe the weather or a plant by my window at my own pace and keep notes.

prompt.zh: 几位朋友自愿办一次很小的聚会，你更想优先照顾哪一项？
prompt.en: Friends voluntarily arrange a very small gathering. Which part would you prefer to attend to?

label.zh: 让空间和招呼方式有温度，也给不想互动的人留余地。
label.en: Make the setting and greetings inviting while leaving room not to interact.

label.zh: 准备一个可自由参加、随时退出的小挑战。
label.en: Prepare a small challenge that people can freely join or leave.

label.zh: 保留可以独处或安静看景的时间，不把全程排满。
label.en: Leave time to be alone or quietly observe the surroundings rather than filling every moment.

label.zh: 把共同确认的时间和分工说清，方便大家按约参加。
label.en: Clarify the agreed time and responsibilities so everyone can participate as arranged.

prompt.zh: 挑选一个新的小爱好时，哪种体验最吸引你？
prompt.en: When choosing a small new hobby, which experience appeals to you most?

label.zh: 有一个难度合适的短练习，可以亲自试一试。
label.en: Having a manageable short exercise I can attempt myself.

label.zh: 自己决定节奏，在可访问的环境里观察自然细节。
label.en: Setting my own pace and observing natural details in an accessible setting.

label.zh: 和愿意参与的人组织一件共同的小事。
label.en: Organising a small shared activity with willing participants.

label.zh: 比较方法、建立步骤，再看怎样改进安排。
label.en: Comparing methods, building steps and considering a better arrangement.

prompt.zh: 为自己策划一个普通的半天，你更想从哪里开始？
prompt.en: You are arranging an ordinary half-day for yourself. Where would you prefer to begin?

label.zh: 先保留不被安排打断的自主时间，再决定去哪里或看什么。
label.en: Keep some self-directed time before deciding where to go or what to observe.

label.zh: 把已答应别人的共同事项确认好，再安排自己的部分。
label.en: Confirm shared commitments I have accepted before arranging my own part.

label.zh: 比较几种路线的时间和条件，选一个合适方案。
label.en: Compare timing and conditions for several routes and choose a suitable plan.

label.zh: 给半天选一个声音、文字或创作主题，随它展开。
label.en: Choose a sound, text or creative theme and let the half-day develop around it.

prompt.zh: 一份自愿参与的通讯需要收尾，你更想接手什么？
prompt.en: A voluntary newsletter needs finishing. Which part would you prefer to take on?

label.zh: 确认哪些内容已经同意发布，协调最后的责任交接。
label.en: Confirm what has been approved for publication and coordinate the final handover.

label.zh: 检查顺序是否清楚，比较读者可能走的阅读路线。
label.en: Check the sequence and compare possible reading routes.

label.zh: 调整版面的留白和措辞，让阅读和交流更舒适。
label.en: Adjust spacing and wording to make reading and responding more comfortable.

label.zh: 集中处理一个明确的小难点，做完后就停下。
label.en: Focus on one clearly bounded difficulty and stop after completing it.

prompt.zh: 整理一次自选活动的记录时，你最想留下哪种内容？
prompt.en: When organising notes from an activity you chose, what would you most like to keep?

label.zh: 不同做法为什么可行，以及下一次可以怎样选择。
label.en: Why different approaches worked and how I could choose next time.

label.zh: 一段有趣的表达，把这次经历变成自己的作品。
label.en: An interesting expression that turns the experience into a small piece of my own.

label.zh: 实际练习过的步骤，以及哪一步需要再试一次。
label.en: The steps I actually practised and one that I might try again.

label.zh: 按自己兴趣发现的小细节，不急着汇成统一结论。
label.en: Small details I noticed through my own interests without rushing to a single conclusion.

prompt.zh: 收到一份没有固定用途的空白本子，你更想怎样开始用？
prompt.en: You receive a blank notebook with no assigned purpose. How would you prefer to begin using it?

label.zh: 写一首短诗、一段旋律记号或一页有节奏的文字。
label.en: Write a short poem, a melody sketch or a page of rhythmic prose.

label.zh: 收集让自己喜欢的配色、纹理和交流片段。
label.en: Collect colours, textures and fragments of conversation I enjoy.

label.zh: 记下自己观察到的季节、光线或植物变化。
label.en: Note changes in seasons, light or plants that I notice for myself.

label.zh: 记录一件共同事项的约定，让职责和决定容易查找。
label.en: Record agreements for a shared activity so responsibilities and decisions are easy to find.

prompt.zh: 共同空间有一面可以临时使用的空墙，你更愿意提出什么？
prompt.en: There is a wall available for temporary use in a shared space. What would you prefer to propose?

label.zh: 做一个温和的视觉角落，先问使用者喜欢怎样的氛围。
label.en: Create a welcoming visual corner after asking users what atmosphere they prefer.

label.zh: 做一个自愿参与的小任务板，难度适中、完成即可移除。
label.en: Make an optional small-task board with manageable challenges that can be removed when done.

label.zh: 先确认大家同意的用途、时限和维护责任。
label.en: First confirm the agreed use, time limit and responsibility for maintenance.

label.zh: 画出不同用途的草图，比较怎样更方便实际使用。
label.en: Sketch alternative uses and compare how they would work in practice.

prompt.zh: 独自去一个熟悉而安全的地方短暂休息，你更想带上什么？
prompt.en: You are taking a short break in a familiar, safe place. What would you prefer to bring?

label.zh: 一件可以随时停止的简短练习材料。
label.en: Materials for a brief practice I can stop at any time.

label.zh: 轻便的观察记录方式，让自己的注意自由停留。
label.en: A light way to record observations while letting my attention move freely.

label.zh: 一页想慢慢比较的方案，不必当场作决定。
label.en: A page of options to compare slowly without needing an immediate decision.

label.zh: 一个可以记下声音、画面或文字灵感的小工具。
label.en: A small tool for recording sounds, images or words that inspire me.

prompt.zh: 朋友邀请你参与一件普通的小创作，你更想怎样贡献？
prompt.en: A friend invites you to join a small, ordinary creative activity. How would you prefer to contribute?

label.zh: 保留自己探索的部分和节奏，再自愿分享所见。
label.en: Keep a part and pace for my own exploration, then share observations if I wish.

label.zh: 和对方确认谁负责什么，以及怎样共同作决定。
label.en: Agree who owns each part and how we will make shared decisions.

label.zh: 想出一种有个人语气的表达，把感觉放进作品。
label.en: Develop an expression in my own voice and put a feeling into the work.

label.zh: 关注作品怎样让人感到被欢迎，以及细节怎样搭配。
label.en: Attend to how the work feels welcoming and how its details fit together.

prompt.zh: 你可以为自愿小组增加一个可选环节，哪一种更合你意？
prompt.en: You can add one optional element to a voluntary group. Which would you prefer?

label.zh: 一个简短的共同约定时段，让责任和决定更清楚。
label.en: A brief time for agreements that clarifies responsibilities and decisions.

label.zh: 一个分享原创短句、旋律或小作品的时段。
label.en: A time to share original lines, melodies or small creations.

label.zh: 一个低风险的小挑战，参与者自行决定做到哪里。
label.en: A low-stakes challenge whose participants decide their own stopping point.

label.zh: 一段可自己选择路线的观察时间，室内也能参加。
label.en: An observation period with self-chosen routes and indoor participation available.

prompt.zh: 遇到一项可以自主安排的普通练习，你更想先照顾什么？
prompt.en: An ordinary practice can be arranged as you wish. What would you prefer to consider first?

label.zh: 先比较两种步骤，看哪一种更适合当前条件。
label.en: Compare two sequences to see which fits the present conditions.

label.zh: 让材料和交流方式有自己喜欢的美感与舒适感。
label.en: Give the materials and communication an aesthetic and comfort I enjoy.

label.zh: 留出独自调整节奏的空间，不必跟别人同步。
label.en: Leave room to set my own pace without needing to match others.

label.zh: 若涉及同伴，先明确各自接受的责任和安排。
label.en: If companions are involved, clarify the responsibilities and arrangements each accepts.

prompt.zh: 看完一个开放的小展览，你更想和朋友聊哪一方面？
prompt.en: After an open small exhibition, which aspect would you prefer to discuss with a friend?

label.zh: 某种声音、叙述或表现形式怎样触动了自己。
label.en: How a sound, narrative or form of expression affected me.

label.zh: 哪一个亲手尝试的环节让自己愿意迎接小挑战。
label.en: Which hands-on element made me want to attempt a manageable challenge.

label.zh: 活动怎样组织、共同规则怎样让参与顺利。
label.en: How the activity was organised and how shared rules supported participation.

label.zh: 展陈路线的取舍，以及另一种设计可能怎样工作。
label.en: The tradeoffs of the display route and how another design might work.

prompt.zh: 准备给自己留一个普通周末的纪念，你更想保留什么？
prompt.en: You want a small keepsake from an ordinary weekend. What would you prefer to keep?

label.zh: 让自己喜欢的色彩和一段有温度的交流。
label.en: Colours I enjoyed and a fragment of a warm conversation.

label.zh: 一段自己选择的安静时间里发现的自然细节。
label.en: A natural detail noticed during quiet time I chose for myself.

label.zh: 一次计划的取舍记录，看看安排怎样影响体验。
label.en: A record of planning tradeoffs and how the arrangement shaped the experience.

label.zh: 一份自己做的小作品，让那天有独特的表达。
label.en: A small creation of my own that gives the day a distinctive expression.

prompt.zh: 一次自选活动将结束，你更想为下一回留下什么？
prompt.en: An activity you chose is ending. What would you prefer to leave for next time?

label.zh: 一个难度刚好的练习目标，保留选择退出的余地。
label.en: A manageable practice target with room to choose not to continue.

label.zh: 清楚的共同约定和交接，避免责任含混。
label.en: Clear shared agreements and a handover that avoids ambiguous responsibilities.

label.zh: 一个还想继续发展的声音、文字或创作点子。
label.en: A sound, text or creative idea I would like to develop further.

label.zh: 一个让人舒服的细节或表达感谢的方式。
label.en: A comfortable detail or a way of expressing appreciation.

prompt.zh: 一个没有外部评分的小项目可以重新开始，你更想怎样做？
prompt.en: A small project with no external grade can be restarted. How would you prefer to approach it?

label.zh: 自己挑选关注的角度，按可行的节奏慢慢探索。
label.en: Choose my own angle of attention and explore at a workable pace.

label.zh: 重新比较几个路径，写清这一回的取舍。
label.en: Compare several routes again and state the tradeoffs for this attempt.

label.zh: 调整配色、材质或交流方式，找到自己喜欢的感觉。
label.en: Adjust colours, materials or communication to find a feeling I enjoy.

label.zh: 挑一个具体可练的部分，尝试后再决定是否继续。
label.en: Choose a specific part to practise and decide whether to continue after trying it.

title.zh: 宙斯：共同安排与责任

headline.zh: 六位神话人物之一的当代偏好联想，不是实际能力结论。
headline.en: A contemporary preference association with one of six myth figures, not an ability verdict.

summary.zh: 从共同约定、协调与承担看本次选择：读一个具体组织例子，比较计划与行动，保留他人同意和自己的责任范围。
summary.en: Explore agreements, coordination and ownership through a concrete organising example, with comparisons that keep consent and responsibility clear.

scoreReading.zh: 18题全部各选一项，对应主题加1，总数固定18。每题从六主题中提供四个，每个主题在全卷出现12次、每位置3次；没有选上的另外两项不记为拒绝。原始次数只是这组可选项中的相对分布，不是独立品质、神祇相似度百分比或人口排名。所有最高计数都保留完整报告；全选第一项会六项各3，全都显示。名单顺序不设主次，相差一次只是一项选择，不证明显著差异、固定主副型或某个特质消失。近分可以一起比较，但不补造未并列的混合类型。换情境或时间可能改变回答，没有常模、稀有度或科学分界。
scoreReading.en: Choose one option for all 18 questions; each adds one to its theme, and counts always sum to 18. Each question offers four of the six themes. Every theme appears 12 times and three times in each position; the two absent themes are not counted as rejected. Raw counts describe relative choices among these options, not independent qualities, god-match percentages or population ranks. Every highest count retains its full guide: choosing the first option throughout gives three each and displays all six. List order establishes no priority. A one-choice gap proves neither significance, fixed primary–secondary types nor the absence of a quality. Compare close results without inventing an untied hybrid type. Context or time may change responses. There are no norms, rarity estimates or scientific cutoffs.

title.zh: 宙斯测试结果：共同安排、具体例子与完整说明
title.en: Zeus Quiz Result: Agreements, Examples and Full Guide

description.zh: 从共同约定、协调与承担看本次选择：读一个具体组织例子，比较计划与行动，保留他人同意和自己的责任范围。
description.en: Explore the Zeus result through agreements, coordination and practical examples. Compare all six themes without claiming leadership or career fit.

title.zh: 神话背景与本版主题
title.en: Mythological background and this edition’s theme

paragraphs.zh: 宙斯在希腊神话中是天空之神和众神之王。本版只借这个统筹联想，写成共同安排和明确责任的原创偏好主题。它不是古代留下的宙斯人格量表，也不把权力、控制、血统或被人服从当成值得追求的品质。
paragraphs.en: Zeus is the sky god and king of the gods in Greek mythology. Here that coordinating association becomes an original theme about shared arrangements and explicit responsibility. This is a contemporary editorial mapping, not an ancient Zeus personality inventory, and power or obedience is not a quality the quiz rewards.

title.zh: 计数怎样联系具体处境

paragraphs.zh: 若这一项计数最高，你在本题组提供的选择里较常优先处理共同约定、职责和决定怎样落地。较少选择可能因为你更想创作、观察或比较方案。可以问自己：我想接手的是协调，还是只是希望当前安排清楚？两种需要不必被同一个名字包住。
paragraphs.en: A highest count means you more often prioritised agreements, responsibilities and how decisions become arrangements among the offered choices. Fewer may reflect a wish to create, observe or compare options instead. Ask whether you want to coordinate or simply want the current arrangement clarified; those needs need not have the same explanation.

title.zh: 一个具体日常例子

paragraphs.zh: 例如，几位朋友自愿组织旧书交换，每个人能投入的时间不同。你可以先确认哪些书能交换、谁愿意在场、谁能收尾，再记录共同决定。协调的具体成果是一份可使用的安排，而不是让每个人听你的。若别人不愿承担某项工作，就重新缩小活动范围。
paragraphs.en: Friends voluntarily organise a used-book exchange with different amounts of available time. Confirm which books can be exchanged, who wants to attend and who can close up, then record the shared decisions. The useful output is a workable arrangement rather than obedience. If nobody accepts a task, reduce the event’s scope instead of assigning it unilaterally.

title.zh: 一句可以怎样说的话
title.en: A possible way to express the preference

paragraphs.zh: 可以说：“我愿意把大家同意的事项整理起来；我能负责登记，收尾还没有人接。我们是缩短时间，还是另找安排？”这把自己的承担、尚未解决的条件和共同选择都说清了。协调之后也可以交接，不必因为开始负责就永远担任组织者。
paragraphs.en: Try: “I can record what we agree and handle registration. Closing up has no volunteer yet. Should we shorten the session or choose another arrangement?” This separates accepted work, an unresolved condition and the group’s choice. A handover remains possible; coordinating the start does not make you the permanent organiser of future gatherings.

title.zh: 和其他五主题怎样比较
title.en: Comparisons with the other five themes

paragraphs.zh: 宙斯主题关注谁共同决定、谁承担；雅典娜主题更关注不同路径为什么合适，阿瑞斯主题更偏向一个亲自尝试的小挑战。三者可以在同一件事里先后出现。阿尔忒弥斯的自主选择也不与负责任冲突，阿波罗的创作和阿芙罗狄蒂的美感交流同样可以帮助合作。
paragraphs.en: The Zeus theme asks who decides together and owns each part. Athena emphasises why a route fits, while Ares emphasises attempting a bounded challenge. All three may appear at different moments. Artemis’s autonomy can coexist with responsibility, and Apollo’s expression or Aphrodite’s aesthetic connection can also contribute to a shared activity.

title.zh: 反例与实际能力的区别

paragraphs.zh: 反例是，一个人把所有任务抓在手里，可能只是分工失灵；另一个人明确拒绝超出范围的责任，仍可能认真守约。问卷没有观察真实组织表现或他人评价，不能由次数推断领导能力、可靠程度、道德或适合管理职业。神话里复杂的权力关系也不是现实相处规范。
paragraphs.en: Taking every task may reflect a broken arrangement rather than good coordination. Declining work outside an agreed scope can also be responsible. These choices observe neither organising performance nor others’ evaluations, so counts establish no leadership skill, reliability, morality or management career fit. Mythological power relationships do not provide rules for contemporary relationships.

title.zh: 可选的小观察

paragraphs.zh: 可选的小观察：为一件原本就要共同完成的小事，分三栏写“已经同意”“我自愿负责”“仍需讨论”。只整理必要信息，不收集私人答卷。看看明确分工是否帮助你表达需要；也可以决定暂不组织。这个记录用于理解选择，不认证你天生适合领导。
paragraphs.en: For an optional observation, take a small activity already planned together and make three columns: agreed, voluntarily mine, and still to discuss. Keep only necessary information, without private answer collection. Notice whether explicit ownership helps express your needs, or decide not to organise. The note explores a preference rather than certifying natural leadership.

title.zh: 神话背景与本版主题
title.en: Mythological background and this edition’s theme

paragraphs.zh: 雅典娜在希腊神话中与雅典、智慧和手工技艺等相联系。本版从中选取比较路径与安排步骤的联想，写成原创普通选择。它没有测知识、推理或工作表现，也不把“理性压过感情”当成正确答案；计划中同样可以包括感受、访问需要和休息。
paragraphs.en: Athena is associated in Greek mythology with Athens, wisdom and crafts. This edition draws a contemporary planning theme from those associations in original everyday choices. It tests no knowledge, reasoning or work performance, and treating feelings as irrelevant is not a correct answer. Plans may include emotions, access needs and rest alongside practical conditions.

title.zh: 计数怎样联系具体处境

paragraphs.zh: 若计数最高，本次较常选择比较办法、辨认条件和说明取舍。你可以进一步区分：是享受思考不同路线，还是因为当前信息不足而暂时需要计划？较少选择也许是已有可用方案，并不说明冲动或不会思考。计数读的是选择次序，不是想得越多就越好。
paragraphs.en: A highest count means you more often chose comparison, relevant conditions and explicit tradeoffs. Distinguish enjoying alternative routes from needing a plan because information is currently missing. Fewer choices may mean a workable plan already exists rather than impulsiveness or inability to think. The tally describes priorities without making more deliberation inherently better.

title.zh: 一个具体日常例子

paragraphs.zh: 例如，你想把一小批资料整理到容易查找，有按日期和按用途两种办法。可以各拿三份试分，比较日常会怎样寻找，再决定保留哪一种。这个例子关心检索任务与分类的关系；不用先把所有资料分析完，也不要求只有一个永远正确的系统。
paragraphs.en: Suppose you want a small collection of notes to be easy to find. Try sorting three by date and three by use, then compare how you would actually retrieve them. This links the method to a practical task without analysing every note first. There need not be one permanently correct system for every future use.

title.zh: 一句可以怎样说的话
title.en: A possible way to express the preference

paragraphs.zh: 可以说：“我想比较这两种办法。我们最常要找的是哪类资料？先用几份试一下，再定是否扩大。”这样把比较的问题、范围和决定点说清。别人需要马上使用时，可以先提供临时入口；计划不是阻止开始的资格，也不必替所有人的需要作判断。
paragraphs.en: You could say, “I’d like to compare these methods. What do we most often need to find? Let’s try a few notes before expanding.” This names the question, scope and decision point. If someone needs immediate access, offer a temporary route. Planning grants no right to delay everyone or decide their needs for them.

title.zh: 和其他五主题怎样比较
title.en: Comparisons with the other five themes

paragraphs.zh: 雅典娜与宙斯都可能参与安排，但前者偏比较路径，后者偏共同决定与职责；这不是智力与权力的对立。阿瑞斯可以先练一个步骤，阿波罗可以调整表达，阿芙罗狄蒂可以照顾美感交流，阿尔忒弥斯可以保留自主观察。它们是题目中的不同优先事项，不是六种互斥的人。
paragraphs.en: Athena and Zeus can both involve arrangements: the former emphasises routes, the latter shared decisions and ownership. They are not an intelligence-versus-power opposition. Ares may try a step, Apollo shape expression, Aphrodite attend to aesthetic connection and Artemis keep autonomous observation. These are priorities among options rather than six mutually exclusive kinds of person.

title.zh: 反例与实际能力的区别

paragraphs.zh: 反例是，一份详细计划可能建立在错误资料上；临时决定也可能来自丰富经验。问卷没有检验方案质量、认知能力或压力反应，不能说雅典娜结果代表更聪明、更公正或适合研究工作。若继续比较已经妨碍实际需要，可以停下或请相关人一起决定，而不是维护原型形象。
paragraphs.en: A detailed plan can rest on wrong information, while a quick decision can draw on experience. No plan quality, cognitive ability or stress response is assessed here. An Athena result certifies neither intelligence, fairness nor research suitability. If continued comparison obstructs a real need, stop or involve the relevant people rather than performing an archetype.

title.zh: 可选的小观察

paragraphs.zh: 可选的小观察：选一件低风险、自己本来就想安排的事，写出两个方案、一个重要条件和停止比较的时点。完成后记录实际发生了什么，不把结果好坏归结为神话类型。你也可以只写出问题，留到有条件时再决定，不新增无必要的任务。
paragraphs.en: If useful, choose a low-stakes matter you already want to arrange. Write two options, one important condition and a point to stop comparing. Later record what actually happened without attributing success or failure to a mythological type. You may simply identify the question and defer a decision until conditions permit, without adding an unnecessary task.

title.zh: 神话背景与本版主题
title.en: Mythological background and this edition’s theme

paragraphs.zh: 阿波罗在希腊神话中与音乐和预言等领域有关。本版只借音乐与表达的联想，把原创声音、文字和小作品写进偏好题。它不测艺术天赋、不预测未来，也不要求站上舞台或被别人欣赏；自己独处时的短小创作同样可以成为表达。
paragraphs.en: Apollo is associated in Greek mythology with music and prophecy, among other domains. Here the musical association informs original preferences about sound, words and small creations. This edition measures no artistic talent and predicts no future. Expression need not involve a stage or audience; a small private creation can matter on its own terms.

title.zh: 计数怎样联系具体处境

paragraphs.zh: 若计数最高，本次较常选择给经历一个个人语气，或把感受放进声音和文字。可以想想：吸引你的是创作过程、节奏、传达某种感觉，还是把普通经历留作纪念？较少选择不说明没有创造力，也许你更想观察、练习或照顾共同安排。
paragraphs.en: A highest count means you more often chose to give an experience your own voice or put a feeling into sound and words. Consider whether you enjoy making, rhythm, conveying a feeling or keeping a memory. Fewer choices establish no lack of creativity; observation, practice or shared arrangements may simply have mattered more here.

title.zh: 一个具体日常例子

paragraphs.zh: 例如，记录一个普通傍晚，不一定要写成完整文章。你可以留下三句文字：一个声音、一个画面和一个当时的感受，再试着改变句子的长短。小作品的价值是你愿意怎样表达这一次经历，而不是证明文字优美、产量足够或值得公开展示。
paragraphs.en: To record an ordinary evening, you need not write a finished essay. Note three lines: a sound, an image and how the moment felt, then try changing their lengths. The small piece concerns how you want to express this experience rather than proving quality, producing enough work or creating something worthy of public display.

title.zh: 一句可以怎样说的话
title.en: A possible way to express the preference

paragraphs.zh: 可以说：“我想用一段很短的声音记住这次活动，还没决定是否给别人听。你愿意只说说听到了什么吗？”这区分创作、是否公开和需要哪种回应。也可以不征求反馈；创作不是持续输出的承诺，休息不会让你失去所谓阿波罗资格。
paragraphs.en: You might say, “I want to remember this through a very short recording and haven’t decided whether to share it. Would you simply describe what you hear?” This separates making, publication and the response wanted. Feedback is optional. A preference for expression creates no commitment to constant output, and resting removes no supposed Apollo qualification.

title.zh: 和其他五主题怎样比较
title.en: Comparisons with the other five themes

paragraphs.zh: 阿波罗主题偏向自己做出一种表达，阿芙罗狄蒂主题更关注美感与交流如何被体验；同一作品可以包含两者。雅典娜的步骤比较、阿瑞斯的短练习也能支持创作，宙斯能处理共同约定，阿尔忒弥斯能保留独自观察。并列可以一起读，不必编一个主次人格。
paragraphs.en: Apollo emphasises making an expression, while Aphrodite attends to experiencing aesthetics and connection; one piece may involve both. Athena’s comparison or Ares’s brief practice may support making, Zeus may handle agreements and Artemis may preserve independent observation. Tied guides can be read together without inventing a primary and secondary personality or ranking the value of their themes.

title.zh: 反例与实际能力的区别

paragraphs.zh: 反例是，有人此刻只想安静欣赏，仍可能有丰富的表达能力；大量创作也不自动代表乐观、魅力或疗愈作用。问卷没有评作品，也没有测试创造力、外向、职业技能或心理健康。不要因为得到这个标签就要求自己感染全场，或把低落看作不符合原型。
paragraphs.en: Someone who wants only to listen may still express themselves richly elsewhere. Producing many pieces guarantees neither optimism, charisma nor healing. No artwork, creativity, extraversion, career skill or mental health is assessed. The label cannot demand that you brighten a room, and feeling low is not a failure to live up to a theme.

title.zh: 可选的小观察

The example concerns an approachable experience. The card need not win praise, produce enthusiasm from everyone or turn every quiet participant into someone who wants to talk.

These items collect no other person’s feelings and observe no relationship. They certify neither empathy, mind-reading, attractiveness, attachment nor partner compatibility, and cannot recommend design or relationship-service careers. The same visible setting can be experienced differently by different people.

paragraphs.en: If useful, change one detail you already wanted to change in a small space you can control, then note your experience. Ask any co-users first, without collecting private evaluations or demanding a response. Enjoyment, dislike and no noticeable change are all possible. This explores aesthetic choices without validating charm or proving that relationships have improved.

paragraphs.en: Ares is the god of war in Greek mythology. This edition does not turn mythological warfare into advice. Instead it makes an original entertainment association with bounded challenges: trying a manageable step that can be paused. Conflict, violence, dominance, physical condition and enduring pain are not qualities rewarded by the questions or required by this theme.

paragraphs.en: A highest count means you more often chose practising a part or learning a process through an attempt. Was the appeal a clear difficulty, seeing one completion or doing rather than discussing at that moment? Fewer choices may reflect rest or another priority, without establishing cowardice, laziness or weak will, or creating a demand to change yourself.

title.zh: 一个具体日常例子

paragraphs.zh: 例如，你自愿学一个普通折纸步骤，可以挑一次折痕练习，先看说明、确认材料，再试一轮。完成或决定停下都算作这次过程的一部分。挑战的边界是材料、时间和自己的意愿，不是和别人比赛，也不是一次不会就必须继续到做对。
paragraphs.en: Suppose you voluntarily learn an ordinary paper fold. Choose one crease to practise, read the instructions, check the material and try one round. Completion and deciding to stop both belong to the process. The boundary comes from materials, time and willingness rather than competition or a requirement to continue until you get it right.

title.en: A possible way to express the preference

paragraphs.zh: 可以说：“我想先试这一小段，五分钟后再决定要不要继续；现在不需要比赛或评价。”这把尝试的范围和退出方式放在前面。如果同伴更想慢慢看说明，可以分开安排。行动不必获得所有人跟随，暂停也不等于输掉挑战或失去原型。
paragraphs.en: Try: “I’d like to attempt this short part, then decide after five minutes whether to continue. I don’t need competition or evaluation.” This puts scope and exit first. A companion may prefer to read slowly; separate arrangements are possible. Action requires no followers, and pausing is not losing a challenge or failing a supposed archetype.

title.en: Comparisons with the other five themes

paragraphs.zh: 阿瑞斯与雅典娜可以分别强调试一个步骤和比较路线，顺序并不固定；熟悉的人也可能先计划。宙斯关注共同职责，阿波罗关注表达，美感交流对应阿芙罗狄蒂，自主观察对应阿尔忒弥斯。它们都不是行动与退缩的等级，全部最高并列可同时保留。
paragraphs.en: Ares and Athena can emphasise attempting a step and comparing routes, in either order; an experienced person may plan first too. Zeus attends to shared responsibility, Apollo to expression, Aphrodite to aesthetic connection and Artemis to autonomous observation. These are not grades of action versus retreat, and every highest tie can remain visible together.

title.zh: 反例与实际能力的区别

paragraphs.zh: 反例是，快速行动可能只是步骤熟悉，延迟尝试也可能是条件尚未安全。题目没有观察运动、危险应对或实际表现，不推断体力、攻击性、勇气、抗压、临床状态或适合军警消防等职业。若某件事让人不舒服，应按实际需要停止，不用分数挑战健康与界限。
paragraphs.en: Quick action may simply reflect familiarity; delaying an attempt may mean conditions are not safe yet. No sport, danger response or actual performance is observed. Counts establish neither fitness, aggression, courage, resilience, clinical state nor suitability for military, police or emergency work. Stop according to actual needs rather than testing health or boundaries against a score.
